first.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous declines in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ). Memory_31 and memory_86 both demonstrate that simplification and shortening of onboarding drives measurable improvements in activation and completion—the exact metrics declining now. We verify these two to confirm the mechanism remains sound. Activation_messaging (memory_91) provides a complementary signal that product-level engagement interventions work. Promotional_pricing (memory_73) would address competitor pressure but explicitly damaged 30-day retention and conflicts with sustainable revenue goal. Referral_incentive works but targets existing customers, not the acquisition/activation problem. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is strong but requires different operational setup. Simplifying onboarding directly targets both observed declines, has durable precedent, and carries no retention risk. Standard_experiment scale allows rapid validation without overcommitment.

final.rationale: Archive verification confirms both memories. Memory_31 shows signup simplification drove +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB with minimal retention risk (-1%). Memory_86 shows shortened onboarding lifted completion +13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention +3%. Current situation exhibits exactly these decay patterns (activation -6% QoQ, completion -4% QoQ). Simplifying onboarding is the highest-confidence action: it directly addresses both observed declines, has proven durable lift on qualified revenue, carries positive retention signal, and avoids the retention damage of promotional_pricing (memory_73) or acquisition-only focus of referral_incentive. Standard_experiment scale enables rapid iteration while protecting against overexposure. This preserves long-term sustainable revenue objective while defending against competitor pressure through product engagement rather than unsustainable pricing.
